title: Text-level coding filter for transformer backends and six-config study
description: Add a text-level variant of the coding-domain neutralization for the transformer backends (applied to the stripped text before tokenization), make the filter a backend option, add a synthetic probe set (ordinary coding phrases plus genuinely negative same-word phrases), and extend the eval harness to run vader, transformer-sst2, and transformer with and without the filter: probe neu/neg split, tuning/held-out/combined accuracy, confusion matrices.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Six-config coding-filter study complete (all synthetic data, aggregate numbers only). Eval: scripts/sentiment-backend-eval.ts now runs every backend with the filter on and off against tuning (36), held-out (28), combined (64) gold plus a 24-probe set (19 technical uses of filter vocabulary + 5 genuinely negative same-vocabulary phrases). Added the text-level filter to the transformer path (same neutralizeCodingTerms word-boundary replace applied before tokenization) and per-backend option plumbing: --sentiment-coding-filter on|off|auto, config key sentimentCodingFilter, auto = per-backend default. Results (accuracy, probes as neu/neg split): vader+filter 1.000/0.462/0.767, probes 0.875 (17/19 neu, 4/5 neg); vader-raw 0.735/0.423/0.600, probes 0.583 (9/19 neu, 5/5 neg); transformer-sst2+filter 0.676/0.346/0.533, probes 0.500 (12/19, 0/5); transformer-sst2-raw 0.676/0.346/0.533 (identical on gold), probes 0.708 (17/19, 0/5); transformer goemotions+filter 0.971/0.731/0.867, probes 0.917 (19/19, 3/5); goemotions-raw 0.971/0.731/0.867 (identical on gold), probes 0.917 (17/19, 5/5). Key finding: gold accuracies byte-identical with and without the filter for goemotions, but the filter flips one genuine-frustration probe neg->neu and another neg->pos (+0.413), so it is redundant and harmful there. Throughput re-measured: vader ~21-45k msgs/sec, sst2 ~435-470, goemotions ~253-263.
